heading: INT. SWIM STADIUM - STARTING BLOCKS - MORNING

units.text: INT. SWIM STADIUM - STARTING BLOCKS - MORNING
Chlorine haze.
A thousand empty seats.
A pool lit like a jewel, eight lanes, seven of them still.
KEIKO TANAKA, 20s, in a black racing suit, swim cap tight, stands behind block four shaking out her arms.
A waterproof earbud sits in one ear.
She presses it and her own voice, recorded the night before, plays back thin and steady.
Hands loose. Shoulders down. You've done this ten thousand times.
units.name: KEIKO

units.text: She steps up.
Toes curl over the edge.
She bounces once on her heels, flexes her fingers, rolls her neck, glances at the empty stands, then at the water, then at the clock above lane eight that reads zero.
Her breath fogs in the cold air.
She presses the earbud again.
Don't think about her. Think about the wall.
units.name: KEIKO

units.text: She pulls the goggles down, snaps the strap, and tucks the earbud deeper.
She lowers into a crouch.
Breathe.
units.name: KEIKO

units.text: A beat.
A horn blares from nowhere.
She dives.
Under the surface there is silence, and then only the sound of her own heart.
